+import re

 from rentomatic.shared.domain_model import DomainModel
 
+ISO_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\Z')
+
+
+def parse_iso_date(value):
+    """Parse an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) into a ``datetime.date``.
+
+    Raises ``ValueError`` when the value is not a string or is not a valid
+    ISO date in strict YYYY-MM-DD format.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not ISO_DATE_PATTERN.match(value):
+        raise ValueError(
+            'Not a valid ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD): {}'.format(value))
+
+    return datetime.strptime(value, '%Y-%m-%d').date()

     def __eq__(self, other):
         return self.to_dict() == other.to_dict()
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def window_overlaps(room_available_from, room_available_to,
+                        requested_from, requested_to):
+        """Return True when a room's advertised availability window overlaps
+        the requested window, boundary dates included.
+
+        All arguments are ISO date strings (YYYY-MM-DD); either bound of the
+        requested window may be None, meaning "unbounded" on that side.
+        A room that does not advertise both ends of its window can never
+        overlap a requested window.
+
+        Raises ``ValueError`` when a provided date is not a valid ISO date.
+        """
+        if room_available_from is None or room_available_to is None:
+            return False
+
+        room_from = parse_iso_date(room_available_from)
+        room_to = parse_iso_date(room_available_to)
+
+        if requested_from is not None and \
+                room_to < parse_iso_date(requested_from):
+            return False
+
+        if requested_to is not None and \
+                room_from > parse_iso_date(requested_to):
+            return False
+
+        return True
+
 
 DomainModel.register(StorageRoom)

+ISO_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\Z')
+
+
+def parse_iso_date(value):
+    """Parse an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) into a ``datetime.date``.
+
+    Raises ``ValueError`` when the value is not a string or is not a valid
+    ISO date in strict YYYY-MM-DD format.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not ISO_DATE_PATTERN.match(value):
+        raise ValueError(
+            'Not a valid ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD): {}'.format(value))
+
+    return datetime.strptime(value, '%Y-%m-%d').date()
+

+    @staticmethod
+    def window_overlaps(room_available_from, room_available_to,
+                        requested_from, requested_to):
+        """Return True when a room's advertised availability window overlaps
+        the requested window, boundary dates included.
+
+        All arguments are ISO date strings (YYYY-MM-DD); either bound of the
+        requested window may be None, meaning "unbounded" on that side.
+        A room that does not advertise both ends of its window can never
+        overlap a requested window.
+
+        Raises ``ValueError`` when a provided date is not a valid ISO date.
+        """
+        if room_available_from is None or room_available_to is None:
+            return False
+
+        room_from = parse_iso_date(room_available_from)
+        room_to = parse_iso_date(room_available_to)
+
+        if requested_from is not None and \
+                room_to < parse_iso_date(requested_from):
+            return False
+
+        if requested_to is not None and \
+                room_from > parse_iso_date(requested_to):
+            return False
+
+        return True

+"""In-process audit trail of storage-room list queries.
+
+This is a REST-layer concern: it records what the HTTP API served and is
+read back through the audit endpoint, so it lives in the REST layer and
+only ever stores plain, JSON-serialisable data (no Flask objects, no
+higher-layer types).
+
+The trail is intentionally module-level state: it has to survive across
+requests within the same server process.
+"""
+
+MAX_RETURNED_ENTRIES = 50
+
+_entries = []
+
+
+def record(timestamp, filters, result_count):
+    """Append one query entry to the trail.
+
+    ``filters`` is copied so that later changes to the caller's dict
+    cannot mutate already-recorded entries.
+    """
+    _entries.append({
+        'timestamp': timestamp,
+        'filters': dict(filters) if filters else {},
+        'result_count': result_count,
+    })
+
+
+def recent_entries(limit=MAX_RETURNED_ENTRIES):
+    """Return up to ``limit`` entries, newest first.
+
+    ``limit=None`` returns the whole trail.
+    """
+    if limit is None:
+        return list(reversed(_entries))
+
+    return list(reversed(_entries))[:limit]
+
+
+def clear():
+    """Empty the trail (used by the test suite)."""
+    del _entries[:]

+"""In-process audit trail of storage-room list queries.
+
+This is a REST-layer concern: it records what the HTTP API served and is
+read back through the audit endpoint, so it lives in the REST layer and
+only ever stores plain, JSON-serialisable data (no Flask objects, no
+higher-layer types).
+
+The trail is intentionally module-level state: it has to survive across
+requests within the same server process.
+"""
+
+MAX_RETURNED_ENTRIES = 50
+
+_entries = []
+
+
+def record(timestamp, filters, result_count):
+    """Append one query entry to the trail.
+
+    ``filters`` is copied so that later changes to the caller's dict
+    cannot mutate already-recorded entries.
+    """
+    _entries.append({
+        'timestamp': timestamp,
+        'filters': dict(filters) if filters else {},
+        'result_count': result_count,
+    })
+
+
+def recent_entries(limit=MAX_RETURNED_ENTRIES):
+    """Return up to ``limit`` entries, newest first.
+
+    ``limit=None`` returns the whole trail.
+    """
+    if limit is None:
+        return list(reversed(_entries))
+
+    return list(reversed(_entries))[:limit]
+
+
+def clear():
+    """Empty the trail (used by the test suite)."""
+    del _entries[:]
